title: Verdict-routed remediation
summary: One remediation stage MUST repair the failures the verify verdict or the release gate recorded, MUST run only blast-radius tests while iterating, MUST leave the fast, integration, and full suites to the gates, and works under a persona and authority the verdict selects: fail_remedial repairs within the ratified plan, fail_severe adds bounded plan-amendment authority.
instructions: Remediation MUST start from the failure evidence the card lists. When a verify verdict routed the run, that evidence is the verdict and every blocking finding. It also includes every failed acceptance criterion or QA case, and the remediation guidance. When a release-gate failure routed the run, that evidence is the recorded full-profile result and its evidence log.
The remediator MUST reproduce each failure before it changes that failure. It MUST dispute a failure it cannot reproduce, with evidence, rather than patch it blindly.
Each remediation entry MUST state the cause from the verify evidence, the action taken, and non-empty proof.
Remediation MUST fix causes, not symptoms, and MUST NOT weaken, skip, or delete tests to make a failure pass.
Under fail_remedial, the stage MUST NOT amend the plan or acceptance criteria. Evidence that the plan itself is wrong is a blocked report for the operator.

Under fail_severe, the stage MAY amend the plan or an acceptance criterion minimally. The stage MUST record the original statement, the amended statement, a justification, and the forcing evidence in data.plan_amendments. Amendments MUST NOT expand scope, remove a criterion, or reverse ratified product intent. Those remain operator decisions.

After each group of repairs, the remediator SHOULD run the impacted iteration profile plus every test it added. In self-development that profile is `pan tests impacted`. In a target installation the remediator MUST use the target's declared impacted profile. Only when no impacted profile exists, the remediator MUST select the tests in the blast radius by judgment. Every test command MUST derive from runtime/repository-checks.json or the target's documented test entry points. The remediator MAY run the static profile freely. The remediator SHOULD run each profile through `pan tests impacted` or `pan repository-check <profile> --run <run-id>`, which print a pass line or the failing tests with the path of the full log. The remediator SHOULD NOT pipe raw suite output into its context.

The impacted mapping does not reach every changed path. When a changed path yields no impacted test, the remediator MUST choose a judgment cohort of tests that cover that path. It MUST NOT treat the empty selection as an absent blast radius. It MUST record each unreached path and its chosen cohort. Cohort selection is judgment-only and carries no deterministic check.

The deterministic gates own the suites. The remediator MUST NOT run the fast profile or the integration lane itself, and MUST NOT run the full profile. When the impacted selection, every test it added, and the static checks pass, the remediator submits. The remediate exit gate and the verify entry refresh rerun every interior gate profile, and a failure returns the run with its log. On that retry the remediator MUST fix the cause and MUST then re-run only the impacted selection, the failing tests, and every test it added. Every other test execution MUST be the impacted profile plus the tests the remediator added. This rule saves worker turns and context, because the gates rerun every profile anyway.

The remediate submission gate MUST NOT run the full profile. A successful remediation returns along the stage's own success transition to verify, whether a verify verdict or a release-gate failure routed it. Verify retakes its evidence at the repaired workspace, and the ship release gate then runs the full profile again.
Before submission, the implementation claims, remediation entries, and referenced artifacts MUST run their resolved policy-bound validators under VALID-001.

The remediator SHOULD read files with the Read and Grep tools in parallel batches, and SHOULD NOT browse files through the shell. The remediator SHOULD edit its stage output with the file-editing tools, and SHOULD NOT edit it with an inline interpreter script. These habits save worker turns and context.

The remediator SHOULD record `data.implementation.handoff` with where the next worker should start, the symbols it changed, its decisions, and what it left unproven. A later source-editing worker receives that handoff with the harness's reading map of the remediator's transcript, and it SHOULD start from them instead of exploring the codebase again. This saves worker turns and context.
